_comment: Trinkets: small curious keepsakes found in pockets, chests and starting kits (Expansion 2 part D; in the spirit of the PHB 2024 Trinkets table, written fresh for Realmwalker). The name is how the item is called in a pack (no a or an).

trinkets.name: tin whistle with no pea
trinkets.text: Someone cut the pea out with a knife. It still makes a thin, wet sound if you blow hard enough.

trinkets.name: two mismatched coat buttons
trinkets.text: One horn, one pewter, both torn off with a scrap of cloth still in the thread. Somebody left in a hurry.

trinkets.name: half a wax seal on a ribbon
trinkets.text: The crest is cut clean through. The other half went to someone who has not yet come to claim the bargain.

trinkets.name: drover's tally stick
trinkets.text: Notched along one edge with the count of beasts lost on the road. The last forty notches are fresher than the rest.

trinkets.name: rat's skull on a bootlace
trinkets.text: A plague-year charm. The jaw is wired shut, so whatever it was meant to say stays unsaid.

trinkets.name: pewter pilgrim's badge
trinkets.text: Stamped with a saint's cart-wheel. Wearing it got a stranger bread and a bed at forty hostels, so they say.

trinkets.name: child's wool shoe, much darned
trinkets.text: Too small for any hand to wear. It has been mended more often than it was ever worn.

trinkets.name: black iron nail from a barrow
trinkets.text: Dug from a grave mound and old past counting. It rusts to red in a day if you leave it out in the rain.

trinkets.name: thimble with a bent rim
trinkets.text: Brass, worn thin on the crown. Inside, scratched fine: the initials of a seamstress and a date eleven winters gone.

trinkets.name: key to no lock you know
trinkets.text: Long, with an ugly bit. The ring on it is worn bright where a gaoler's thumb sat for years.

trinkets.name: stub of a funeral candle
trinkets.text: Black wax, stamped with a sign of the grave-guild. Half burnt, then pinched out by someone who wanted it for later.

trinkets.name: string of eleven milk teeth
trinkets.text: Threaded on gut. Whose they are, and why a parent would part with them, is not for the string to say.

trinkets.name: three bone dice, all weighted
trinkets.text: Each throws a six more often than luck allows. The owner scratched a tiny cross on the one that always comes up one.

trinkets.name: lead guild token, defaced
trinkets.text: A tanners' mark, scored across with a knife. A man who was thrown out of his trade wore this next to his skin.

trinkets.name: hand's length of hangman's rope
trinkets.text: Greased with tallow at the knot. They sell it at fairs, and nobody who sells it will say where it came from.

trinkets.name: slate scratched with half a psalm
trinkets.text: A novice's penance, left unfinished. The writing gets crooked towards the end, as if the hand was shaking.

trinkets.name: silver spoon, bent double
trinkets.text: Someone tried to bite it to see if it was true. It was, and the tooth marks are still in the bowl.

trinkets.name: wolf's claw bound in sinew
trinkets.text: Hung from a drover's belt against the night. The sinew is new, and the claw is not.

trinkets.name: corner of a faded banner
trinkets.text: Red once, torn from a flag nobody would admit to losing. The edge is scorched and smells of old smoke.

trinkets.name: pocket salt cellar of horn
trinkets.text: The stopper is stitched on with a hair. Those who were in the siege will not let anyone waste a grain.

trinkets.name: tax receipt for a village that burned
trinkets.text: Paid in full, with a clerk's flourish. The roll it came from has long since gone up the chimney.

trinkets.name: the lid of a small clay ewer
trinkets.text: Glazed green, chipped on one side. It fits no jar you have found, and you keep hoping it will.

trinkets.name: ship's biscuit, hard as slate
trinkets.text: Stamped with a captain's name. It has outlasted the ship, the captain, and the weevils that ate the rest.

trinkets.name: map of rivers that are not there
trinkets.text: Beautifully drawn on scraped hide, with the towns named in a hand that wrote them in wishful thinking.

trinkets.name: straw doll with a knotted waist
trinkets.text: Left at a field's edge at harvest, for luck. Someone took it instead of leaving it, and is probably unlucky now.

trinkets.name: bell's clapper, cracked
trinkets.text: Forged iron, as long as your hand. The bell it belonged to was melted for cannon, they say, or for a crown.

trinkets.name: ring plaited from grey hair
trinkets.text: Tied off with a brass band. It is worn by widows of the river towns, and by those who wish to look like one.

trinkets.name: lead toll chit for a fallen bridge
trinkets.text: Good for one crossing. The bridge is now two stumps, and you would have to pay the river instead.

trinkets.name: tin of rusty fish hooks
trinkets.text: Hand-forged and mostly useless, wrapped in oiled wool. On the lid someone has scratched: for Da, for the lake.

trinkets.name: goose quill cut for left hands
trinkets.text: The nib is stained brown with oak gall. Whoever used it wrote a great deal, none of it kind.

trinkets.name: the spectacles of a dead scholar
trinkets.text: One lens is cracked, the other clouded. They were pulled out of a book that someone else wanted to read.

trinkets.name: nail-holed horseshoe, quite small
trinkets.text: Off a pony's foot. Hung over a door in a town you passed through, and stolen before the first frost.

trinkets.name: five sheep knucklebones in a bag
trinkets.text: Polished smooth by children's hands. They play a game with them across half the country, and each place has other rules.

trinkets.name: hollow ring that never held poison
trinkets.text: The lid is neat and the secret compartment empty. Whoever bought it paid for a drama that never came.

trinkets.name: sealed letter with nothing in it
trinkets.text: The wax is sound and the address is clear. Open it and there is only a single hair, a pressed flower, and an apology.

trinkets.name: rusted wrist-shackle, hinged
trinkets.text: No key was ever kept for this one. It has been cut open, and someone has dressed the edges smooth with a file.

trinkets.name: knotted cord of nine colours
trinkets.text: Tied by a hedge woman for a sailor's wind. Seven of the knots are undone, and the sea is not close.

trinkets.name: copper coin that stays cold
trinkets.text: Stamped with a king whose name is not in any chronicle you know. It is cold in the sun and colder beside a fire.

trinkets.name: three gravedigger's measuring pegs
trinkets.text: Hazel, notched at the height of a child, a woman and a man. The last is rubbed smooth with use.

trinkets.name: prayer rope of forty-one knots
trinkets.text: One short of the proper count. A mistake, say some; the missing knot is a vow, say others.

trinkets.name: shoe sole cut from a deserter's boot
trinkets.text: Still stitched with the regimental thread. It has a coin inside the heel, spent long ago, and a place worn for it.

trinkets.name: raven's flight feather, waxed
trinkets.text: Carried by a man who said the birds followed him from a battlefield, and would again.

trinkets.name: rushlight dipped in lamp tallow
trinkets.text: Cheap and smoky and exactly what the poor burn. This one has a thumbprint pressed into the base.

trinkets.name: iron wedding band, too wide
trinkets.text: Worn on a hand that did hard work. The inside is engraved with a date and a single initial, and no second one.

trinkets.name: pair of tiny apothecary scales
trinkets.text: Brass, one pan missing and replaced with a limpet shell. It weighs wrong, and the owner knew it.

trinkets.name: cord of knots from a plague house
trinkets.text: Tied by the watch to count the dead behind a door. Twelve knots, one cut out and kept in a pocket.

trinkets.name: the oath of a company that disbanded
trinkets.text: A paper signed by thirty hands, nine of them crosses. The captain's name has been cut out neatly with a razor.

trinkets.name: beggar's horn cup with a split lip
trinkets.text: It holds a mouthful of water, and not much more. The rim is black where a thousand lips have been.

trinkets.name: awl with a birch handle
trinkets.text: Used by a tanner for thirty years. His grip is worn into the wood, and your hand fits it worse than his did.

trinkets.name: little bell off a lead goat
trinkets.text: Tarnished green and cracked across the mouth, so it clanks rather than rings. A herd followed it into a snowstorm once.

trinkets.name: half a whetstone, worn hollow
trinkets.text: Grey river stone. The hollow is the shape of one blade only, and it is a very good shape.

trinkets.name: violet pressed in a psalter leaf
trinkets.text: The flower is brown and flat as paper. The page it marks is the one about the quiet water.

trinkets.name: sailor's sailcloth needle, three-sided
trinkets.text: Tipped with a brass thimble-guard. It has gone through canvas, flesh and, once, a dead man's eyelid.

trinkets.name: iron earring, cut at the lobe
trinkets.text: Torn from an ear in a hurry. The piece of lobe has long since rotted, but the blood stain has not.

trinkets.name: pouch of seed grain nobody planted
trinkets.text: Rye, still good. The farmer who carried it fled a field he would not see again, and could not bear to eat it.

trinkets.name: the brass cap of a reeve's staff
trinkets.text: Stamped with the shire's mark. A reeve is dead, or disgraced, or both, and his stick did not stay in one piece.

trinkets.name: veil of black gauze, burned at one hem
trinkets.text: Fine enough to see through. It smells of a hearth, and the fire that took the hem did not take the woman.

trinkets.name: four clay marbles, glazed blue
trinkets.text: Fired in a village kiln that closed. One is chipped. All of them are warm, from being held in a fist.

trinkets.name: small watchman's rattle
trinkets.text: Wooden, with a cracked frame. It makes a sound like dry bones in a sack, and so the watch kept it.

trinkets.name: empty boot-knife sheath, sewn twice
trinkets.text: The leather is oiled and old. The blade went long ago, and the sheath was never replaced, for luck or grief.

trinkets.name: hand-carved ox, no longer than a thumb
trinkets.text: Whittled from pine in a long winter. The horns were snapped off once, then glued back with a tar that smells still.

trinkets.name: stoppered vial of dried red ink
trinkets.text: Church ink, ground from cinnabar. Add water and you could sign a bull of excommunication, or a very costly bill.

trinkets.name: coin laid on a dead eye
trinkets.text: Pitted silver, pressed flat on one side. The undertaker who used it forgot to take it back.

trinkets.name: razor with the blade broken off
trinkets.text: Horn handle, hinge still stiff. A barber's mark is cut into the haft, and a second, smaller one beneath it.

trinkets.name: stoppered bottle of nails and hair
trinkets.text: A hedge-folk warding, buried under thresholds. The cork is wax-sealed and warm, from being near a hearth.

trinkets.name: river stone with a hole worn through
trinkets.text: Hung over the stable door against the mare-hag. The cord is new, but the stone is older than the stable.

trinkets.name: leper's wooden clapper
trinkets.text: Two boards on a thong, to warn others off. The wood is smooth with a dead man's grip, and no one wants it.

trinkets.name: clipped crown-penny
trinkets.text: Shaved at the rim until the king's head is a thumb-smear. The clipper made a living from it, and a rope took it.

trinkets.name: the horn tip of a shepherd's crook
trinkets.text: Rubbed pale at the crook. A crack runs through it where a shepherd used it to hit a wolf, or a man.

trinkets.name: two copper rings on one string
trinkets.text: One is for a hand and one is for a finger smaller than any you know. The string is replaced every spring.

trinkets.name: brick from a gaol wall, name scratched
trinkets.text: Someone spent a month scratching it with a spoon handle. The name is Alys, and the date is not finished.

trinkets.name: pocket sundial that tells wrong time
trinkets.text: Brass, with a gnomon bent in a fall. It was accurate once, in some other country, at some other latitude.

trinkets.name: greasy deck of forty cards
trinkets.text: Hand-painted, one queen missing. The painted knave bears a sad likeness to the last man who held them.

trinkets.name: small jar of woad paste, half dry
trinkets.text: Blue as a bruise, and sold to the tribes by the pot. Smear it on and you will look like the dead, or the dangerous.

trinkets.name: stag-horn pin for a cloak
trinkets.text: Carved with the antlers of a beast that is not a stag. The maker's thumb is pressed into the head, twice.

trinkets.name: note written on sausage skin
trinkets.text: It says only: forgive me. The hand is a butcher's, the ink is blood, and nobody can say whom it was for.

trinkets.name: reed flute with seven holes
trinkets.text: The rain-callers of the plain play these. The sixth hole is plugged with wax, and the tune is not the same.

trinkets.name: tin candle mould, one wick-hole
trinkets.text: A chandler's old mould, still greased inside. It is the size of the last candle anyone burned for a drowned son.

trinkets.name: clay pipe, stem bitten through
trinkets.text: Soldier's pipe, with the regiment's number on the bowl. The bite marks go right down to the clay.

trinkets.name: blue glass bead from a barrow
trinkets.text: Round and perfect. A wife put it in a king's mouth, they say, and a grave robber put it in his own.

trinkets.name: coffin nail, bent by an unwilling hand
trinkets.text: Hammered double in a hurry. Whoever took it out of a lid was afraid of what was beneath it, or afraid of what was not.

trinkets.name: rolled lead tablet of names
trinkets.text: Pressed into a well or a wall by some wronged soul. The names are a family's, and each is struck through twice.

trinkets.name: sachet of rue and mugwort
trinkets.text: Sewn into a pillow against bad dreams. The linen is brown with sweat, and the herbs crumble when you smell them.

trinkets.name: stung scrap of beekeeper's veil
trinkets.text: Netting stained with honey and dried welts of old stings. It has the unmistakable smell of smoke and hive.

trinkets.name: fox tail tied to a belt-loop
trinkets.text: The red is going grey. A hunter took it and wore it for a luck that was owed him by a very particular fox.

trinkets.name: bargeman's lead token, wave-stamped
trinkets.text: Pays one passage on the up-river barges. The ferry company ended and the barges rotted, but the token remains.

trinkets.name: finger bone in a quill case
trinkets.text: Sold as a saint's, along with two hundred others. It is probably a pig's, but the box is very well made.

trinkets.name: purse sewn shut with fine thread
trinkets.text: Empty when you shake it. The stitches are so careful and so even that you do not wish to cut them.

trinkets.name: lady's glove, left hand only
trinkets.text: Fine kid, moth-eaten at the cuff. The right hand is somewhere in someone else's pocket, and so is the lady.

trinkets.name: coil of lamp wick, singed
trinkets.text: A miner's reserve wick, kept dry in a tin. He did not use it in the dark, and the tin is crushed.

trinkets.name: cloth strip with a red-stitched name
trinkets.text: Sewn into collars so the dead may be known. This one has been unpicked and taken, and nobody knows whose it was.

trinkets.name: comb of antler, three teeth missing
trinkets.text: Carved with a running hare. The teeth were broken in a fight, and nobody mended it, because the hair is gone.

trinkets.name: scrap of gold leaf in a folded page
trinkets.text: Thin as breath. A monk was laying it on a saint's halo when a raid came, and the saint went unfinished.

trinkets.name: hangman's perquisite penny
trinkets.text: He gets to keep the clothes and the coin. This penny has a little hole where a rope-end was threaded.

trinkets.name: plaited whip lash with a lead tip
trinkets.text: Black with years of sweat. A carter's pride and an ox's fear, and it has no handle left.

trinkets.name: knob of bog butter in a birch bark
trinkets.text: Pale, waxy, older than anyone's grandmother. A moor man buried it for the dead and you dug it up.

trinkets.name: dressed stone with a mason's mark
trinkets.text: A tiny square, carved with a hook and two lines. Some cathedral is missing this stone and nobody has noticed.

trinkets.name: fever-charm bag, damp with sweat
trinkets.text: Stuffed with red wool and a dried toad. A child wore it round the neck through a long summer, and lived.

trinkets.name: tavern chalk and a cracked slate
trinkets.text: A debt of sixty pints is chalked there, in a hand that shakes. Beside it, someone has drawn a small gallows.

trinkets.name: scorched child's primer
trinkets.text: The alphabet, a prayer, and a bestiary of beasts that never lived. Half the pages are charred and half are chewed.
